newsitem.title: USA: Frederick Brewing sees Q2 loss, sales up.
newsitem.headline: Frederick Brewing sees Q2 loss, sales up.

text.p: Frederick Brewing Co said Monday it expects to post a second quarter loss of about $650,000 despite expectations that sales will beat last year's quarter by 93 percent.
In a press release, chief executive officer Kevin Brannon also said the craft brewer expects to break even on a monthly basis by the end of the third quarter in September.
Brannon said second quarter sales of the company's craft beers should reach $850,000 for the second quarter versus $440,000 in the 1996 quarter.

Still, higher production and labor costs associated with the opening of a new brewing facility this spring will lead to a quarterly loss about even with its 1997 first quarter loss of more than $645,000, Brannon said in a phone interview. Last year's second quarter loss was about $321,000, or $0.16 per share.
Brannon said he did not have a per share loss estimate for the second quarter yet because shares outstanding have risen.

The brewer expects to have the new facility completely operational by the end of the month, allowing it to significantly cut labor costs, Brannon said. At present, some of the automated equipment is not on line.
